About

The project

The PBM Database

The PBM Database is an independent, long-term resource that brings together published photobiomodulation research. It includes studies indexed under related terms such as low-level laser therapy and red or near-infrared phototherapy, making a dispersed literature easier to find in one place.

The database and this website are a personal project developed as a hobby, without a commercial purpose. They aim to support researchers with literature searches and a view of PBM beyond individual specialties, while helping non-specialist readers follow the research and its development.

Another aim is to identify opportunities to improve PBM research. Recording recurring methodological and reporting issues can help reveal gaps and inform better study design and reporting, contributing to stronger evidence over time.

Where source records provide them, entries include the condition studied, study type, model, country and treatment parameters. Readers can use these details to compare studies, explore the volume of research across conditions and follow how the field is developing.

The database was started in January 2016 and has been updated regularly since. It is manually curated, rather than a formal systematic review. Much of this website’s factual content is drawn from its data; the site’s visual structure was created with AI assistance.

The site also includes nearly 300 pages describing the state of research on individual conditions. These summaries were prepared largely with GPT-6 Luna under the site administrator’s supervision, using studies listed in the PBM Database as source material.

How studies are found and recorded

PubMed searches combine core terms such as “LLLT” and “photobiomodulation” with a broad range of related phrases, treatment and light-source terms, and wavelengths. Broad searches can return many unrelated papers, so candidate records are reviewed manually for relevance.

Forward-citation checks in Google Scholar help find newer papers that cite older, influential PBM work, including Karu (2005). Daily PubMed saved-search alerts are another way new papers are found. This is an ongoing process and may not identify every relevant study.

When information is available in the source papers, records may include structured details and curator-entered markings about study methods, light delivery, comparisons, cautions, or notable findings. These markings describe information recorded in the database; they are not independent ratings of study quality, and their counts can overlap.

The creator

Vladimir Heiskanen

Vladimir Heiskanen is a Finnish dentist and creator of the PBM Database. He began collecting PBM research after writing about red and near-infrared light for a Finnish health blog. In 2013, he published an overview of studies across health conditions and began building the database in 2016.

His publications include peer-reviewed reviews and WALT position papers on photobiomodulation, a systematic review of PBM for cancer-treatment-related salivary gland dysfunction, and work on blue and green light and sunlight. Some have received substantial citations.

In 2026, the World Association for Photobiomodulation Therapy (WALT) awarded him the WALT Prize for his database work. He also serves on the board of Skepsis ry in Finland and has taken part in public fact-checking and critical examination of health claims.
